Codes and links that let any cup be followed back to its plot.

Start Before the first record

What it is

Roast keeps the records of a coffee from the plant to the cup. A grower writes down each day's picking, a processor each step from cherry to green, a roaster each roast, a brewer or taster each cup. Each record points to the one before it, so any cup can be followed back to the plot where it grew.

It runs in your phone's web browser. There is nothing to download from an app store, and no account is needed to start.

Seen fromRoast at a glance

What it is · See how one coffee's records link up

Every record sits somewhere on this path. You use only the part you need: a home brewer may only ever touch the last two, a grower who sells cherry only the first two.

  1. Plot
  2. Harvest
  3. Process run
  4. Green lot
  5. Roast
  6. Cup

Each arrow is a link the app keeps for you. A green lot made from a run knows its run; the run knows its harvests; the harvests know their plots. Nothing is typed twice.

Seen fromRoast at a glanceKilos carry forward

Why it matters

A buyer, a café or a visitor may ask where a coffee came from and how it was made. When each record points to the one before, the answer is already there.

Seen fromRoast at a glanceRecords you can trust

Step 7 · Add something new from anywhere

The bar at the bottom stays in reach of your thumb. New adds a harvest, process run, reading, green lot, roast, brew or cup, colour reading or plot. Find opens Find. Home goes home. Scan reads a KoffyKraft QR with the camera, or from a saved photo or screenshot.

Seen fromYour first day, step 7Finding your way

Step 8 · Find a plot, lot or code

Type in the Find box on Home or Now, or tap Find. Type part of a name or a code. Your records come first, each with its kind on the right. Tap one to open it. Under the results: Searched on this phone. Works with no signal.

Seen fromYour first day, step 8Finding your way

Why it matters

Codes and names are how records find each other. When a lot comes up after three letters, a buyer's question gets answered standing in the store room.

Seen fromYour first day

Plot Where it grows

What it is

Every other record points back to a plot. A harvest names the plots it was picked from; a run takes its cherry from harvests; a green lot comes from a run. Add the estate and its plots once, and every bag can be traced back to the ground it grew on.

Seen fromEstates and plotsGetting set up

Step 2 · Add my estate

Tap + Estate. Only the Estate name * is needed; add the Village / locality, District, State / region, Country and Total area if you like. Further down, the producer's Postal address, Phone and Email are what a European buyer asks for. Tap Save.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 2Getting set up

Step 3 · Add a plot

Tap + Plot. Pick the estate, give a Block if you use them, and a Plot name / code * such as U1. Save, then open the plot again to fill in the rest at your own pace.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 3Getting set up

What it is

An open plot shows a short summary (variety, species, area, last harvest) and buttons that jump to each part: Location, Land check, Plants, Soil, Flowering, Plot and cup, Map, Rows and Photos. Below them, the chain: the harvests picked here, and what came of them.

Seen fromEstates and plotsFinding your way

Step 4 · Put a plot on the map

Stand in the plot and tap Use my location. The latitude and longitude fill in, with how sure the phone is (in metres). For the exact shape, tap Mark outline on map: chapter "Map" below shows how.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 4

Watch out

A plot of 4 hectares or more needs its outline, not only a point: the plot says so in red. Buyers in Europe ask for the outline of large plots.

Seen fromEstates and plotsGuidance, not guarantee

Step 5 · Check a plot against forest maps

With a location or outline saved, tap Run land check. The app compares the plot with the EU's map of forest at the end of 2020 and with tree loss since, and shows the result, the date and the sources. Each check is kept; the newest shows first.

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 5Guidance, not guarantee

What it is

Plot and cup gathers the cup scores of green lots and roasts made from this plot, beside your other plots. Over seasons it shows which plots and practices give better cups.

Seen fromEstates and plotsQuality as you go

Step 9 · Mark an area on the map

Open Map. Mark an area lets you tap each corner of a plot, then finish; area and height are worked out. Walk the edge records the outline as you walk it. Add a spot marks a store, a drying yard, a house or a water source. Measure gives a distance. Save and share as a GeoJSON file, a KML file (Google Earth) or a printed sheet.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 9

Step 10 · Walk and record a trail

Open Trails and tap ● Start a trail. Allow location, pick what the trail is (a path, a road, a drain, a boundary, the rows of plants), and walk. Add a photo or a stop with a note on the way. Finish when you are done: distance, time and climb show.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 10Nothing gets lost

Step 11 · Map the rows and number the plants

Open Rows and pick the plot. Add a row in any of four ways:

  • ✏️ Draw a row on the map
  • 🚶 Walk a row with the phone
  • 📍 Row ends (GPS)
  • 〰️ From a trail walked up and down the rows

Give the spacing, and each plant gets a number and a label such as R3-12. Tap a plant to mark it healthy, weak, sick, dead, a gap or replanted.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromEstates and plots, step 11

Harvest The day's picking

What it is

A harvest says what was picked, where and when. Later a process run takes its cherry from one or more harvests, and the green lot it makes points back through them to the plots. You need at least one plot first; if you have none yet, save the harvest now and tick its plots later.

Seen fromLogging a harvest

Step 2

Tap + Harvest. The Harvest code and Date are filled in. The code is made from the date: H, then year, month and day, then a number for the day (H261102-1 is the first harvest on 2 November 2026).

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromLogging a harvest, step 2

Step 3 · Say which plots were picked

Change the Date if you picked on another day (Start time and End time are optional). Under Plots picked, tick each plot. Choose the Picking (Selective, Strip, Gleaning or Mixed) and the number of Pickers.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromLogging a harvest, step 3

Process run Cherry to green

What it is

A run follows one batch through floating, pulping, fermentation, washing, drying, resting and hulling. It takes its cherry from your harvests, so it already knows the plots, and the green lot made at the end takes its weight from the run.

Seen fromProcess runsKilos carry forward

Step 1 · Start a processing run

Open Origin, the Process tab, and tap + Process. The Process code is made from the date (P, then year, month and day).

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromProcess runs, step 1

Step 3 · Take the cherry from my harvests

Under Source harvests, tick the harvests in this batch; each shows its code, date and kilos. Cherry in adds up. For cherry not logged as a harvest, leave them unticked and type the kilos in Cherry in (if not from harvests). Check Started.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 3Kilos carry forward

Step 10

The run's page shows the chain from plot to harvest to this run, and Share to a space, Image or PDF and Passport and QR.

Seen fromProcess runs, step 10

Green lot What goes to the roaster

What it is

A green lot is what goes to the roaster. Your own coffee points back to its run, and through it to the harvests and plots. Bought coffee keeps its origin as the seller states it. Every roast later picks a green lot as its source, and the stock goes down by itself.

Seen fromGreen lotsKilos carry forward

Step 1 · Make a green lot from my run

Open Origin, the Green tab, and tap + Green lot. The Green lot code is made from the date (G, then year, month and day). Give it a Name people will recognise.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 1

Step 2

Under From process, pick the run. Its chain shows, and a message: Green weight filled from the run, with the kilos from the run's last Out kg. Change it if the scale says otherwise.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 2Kilos carry forward

Step 5

Tap Save. The lot's page shows its chain back to plot, harvest and run, how much is left, and This lot, Quality and stock, EUDR, Sack labels and For a buyer.

Seen fromGreen lots, step 5

Step 6 · Record coffee I bought in

For bought coffee, leave From process empty and fill Bought coffee: origin as the seller states it. The boxes are Farm or washing station, Producer, Region, Country, Variety, Process, Altitude, m, Harvest, Bought from, Lot or auction number, Invoice date. Use the words on the seller's papers.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 6

Watch out

A lot with no process and nothing under Bought from still saves, with a message: Not linked to a process. Pick its process, or fill Bought from to mark it bought in. Without one of the two, nobody can tell where it came from.

Seen fromGreen lotsRecords you can trust

Step 9 · Print sack labels

Tap Sack labels: one 100 by 50 mm label per bag, with a QR, the lot code, name and estate, process, moisture, date and Bag 1 of 1. Tap Print at the top. The QR opens this lot in the app; once the lot has a passport, it opens the passport, which anyone can check.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromGreen lots, step 9

Tip

If the labels do not open, the phone may be blocking pop-ups for the app. Allow them and tap Sack labels again.

Seen fromGreen lots

Passport What a buyer can check

What it is

A lot passport is a public page for one lot, with a QR for the bag. It shows the chain from plot to harvest, run, green lot and roast. Each entry is signed by the phone that made it and linked to the one before, and each day's entries are stamped into the Bitcoin public record through OpenTimestamps. Anyone who scans the QR sees every check run in their own browser.

Seen fromPassports and selling into EuropeRecords you can trust

Step 2 · Make a passport for a lot

Open the green lot in Origin and tap Passport and QR at the top (you need to be signed in). The app lists every record it is about to seal, from the estate down to this lot.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 2

Step 4 · Seal it

Tap Sign and seal. Each record is signed on this phone and linked to the one before. You will see the lot's page: its public link with Copy link, Print labels and Open passport, and a line saying whether all entries check out and the weights add up.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 4Records you can trust

Step 7 · Split a lot into retail packs

Under Packs, Split into packs: how many, grams each, and whether they come from roasts or stock held. Each pack gets its own QR, and pack weights are checked against what was roasted or held.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 7Kilos carry forward

Step 8 · Send a lot to a buyer

Under Hand over, type the Buyer email, a name to show if you like, and the Weight sent, kg, then tap Sign and send. The buyer confirms on their own phone the weight they received, and can add their own roasts to the same passport. Their email is only used to reach them, never shown.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 8Kilos carry forward

What it is

The EU deforestation rule (EUDR) covers coffee sold into Europe. Each lot must come from land where no forest was cleared after 31 December 2020, must be grown under the country's laws, and must be traceable to the plots it grew on. The company that brings it into Europe files the due diligence statement; your part is to hand over complete, true records. The app's EUDR guide explains this in plain words.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromPassports and selling into EuropeGuidance, not guarantee

Step 10 · See what a lot still needs for Europe

Open the green lot and tap EUDR. The app names any plot data still missing (a location, an outline). It also holds the Product form, the HS code it suggests from the form (the customs code for the goods), and the importer's statement reference once they file it.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 10Guidance, not guarantee

Step 11 · Gather everything a buyer asks for

Tap For a buyer on the lot. One sheet gathers the lot passport, the EUDR lot file, the EU plot file and sack labels.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 11

Step 12 · Make the EUDR lot file

From For a buyer, open the EUDR lot file. On one page, made from your records, it shows the lot, the product, quantity, when and where it was produced, the plots, the producer and the land check. Missing items show in red. Print or save as PDF to send it.

Seen fromPassports and selling into Europe, step 12Guidance, not guarantee

Watch out

The EU plot file holds the exact plot outline. Share it only with the buyer who needs it. Wages and workers' names never go into these files.

Seen fromPassports and selling into EuropeRecords you can trust

Roast Heat and time

What it is

A roast that names its green lot carries the lot's chain with it: plot, harvest, run and lot. The lot's stock goes down by the green weight you roast, and the roast shows on the lot and on its passport.

Seen fromRoastingKilos carry forward

Step 2 · Say which coffee I am roasting

In the timer, under Roaster and coffee identity, pick the Source green lot. The estate, coffee code and moisture fill in from the lot. Add the Roast number, the Green weight g, the Charge temperature °C and your Machine / roaster profile if you like.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRoasting, step 2Kilos carry forward

Cup Brew, cup and taste

What it is

A brew that names its roast joins the coffee's chain: plot, harvest, run, green lot, roast, cup. Over time you can see which roasts and which recipes gave the cups you liked.

Seen fromBrewing and cuppingQuality as you go

Step 2 · Write down the recipe

Pick the Roast from your Roastbook, or type the Coffee (if not from a roast here). Choose the Method * (V60, AeroPress, espresso, South Indian filter and many more). Then fill what you used: Coffee g, Water g (espresso: yield g), Water °C, Grinder and Grind setting, bloom, total time and pours.

Seen fromBrewing and cupping, step 2Quality as you go

Business People, work, sales, land

Step 5 · Record a sale

Open Sales and money and tap ＋ Sale. Pick the buyer and product from your lists, the quantity and the rate; the amount works itself out. A green lot can fill it. The buyer's GSTIN and credit days show, and the payment due date fills in. Dispatch, inside the sale, keeps the transporter, vehicle, e-way bill, freight and dates.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 5Kilos carry forward

Step 11 · Compare one coffee with others

Open Shared spaces (an account is needed). Give the space a Name, and optionally the Coffee (optional) everyone is using, and tap Create space. Invite people by email; each adds a copy of their own brews, roasts, cuppings or process runs, and everyone comments. The owner can turn on a read-only public link.

Try it in the app ›

Seen fromRunning the business, step 11Quality as you go

Open a plot, harvest, run or green lot and tap Image or PDF: an Instagram post, a story or a PDF, drawn on your phone with your profile name, logo and colour. Notes and GPS location are left out unless you switch them on.
